newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to complain over U.S. beef delay - Sola.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to complain over U.S. beef delay - Sola.

text.p: Argentina will lodge a formal complaint to the United States over reported further delays in its approval of a 20,000 tonne fresh beef export quota, Agriculture Secretariat Felipe Sola said Wednesday.
Sola said Argentina understood unofficially that the U.S. government has decided to apply legislation designed to protect small firms to the approval process for the quota.
"This seems to be worth a protest despite our not having been informed officially," Sola told a news conference.
The decision to apply the legislation would mean a 60-day period to consider whether to authorize the quota before it could be voted on in the U.S. Congress, he said.

Sola said he had complained to Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella and Argentina would write to U.S. congressmen to protest. He said the United States did not apply the legislation when it authorised a similar quota for Uruguayan beef and that the small size of the quota meant that U.S. businesses were not threatened.
Sola said that the United States had first agreed to authorize Argentine beef imports three years ago, and that Argentina was losing patience.
"The Secretariat does not rule out complaining to the World Trade Organization," he said, although he added that it was unlikely to prove necessary.
"If this went on longer than August, we would go to the World Trade Organization," he added.

Officials from both the United States and Argentina said in April that the United States could lift its 67-year old ban on fresh beef imports from Argentina in May, ending a two-year wait for approval.

The 20,000 tonne quota which Argentina said has been promised by the United States -- on the condition of achieving U.S. Department of Agriculture sanitary approval -- would not in itself significantly boost Argentina's beef exports. But it is seen as symbolically vital for gaining access to coveted Asian markets, especially Japan and South Korea.
Argentine beef was long barred from major markets because of foot-and-mouth disease in its herd, but the government says three years have passed since the last outbreak.
Argentina exported about 500,000 tonnes of beef in both 1996 and 1995.
